simple.meaning: פָּרַר (pârar) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to break up (usually figuratively), i.e. to violate , frustrate.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 50 times in Genesis, Leviticus, Numbers, Deuteronomy, Judges, and 13 more, beginning at Genesis 17:14. The surrounding contexts include covenant, commandment, land.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to פָּרַר (H6565) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: פָּרַר (pârar) / H6565 is traced through Genesis 17:14, Leviticus 26:15, Leviticus 26:44, Numbers 15:31 with source-language evidence and verse context.
